chapterTitle: FBISE Model Paper 1 (Section A Simulator - Units 1-5)
subject: physics-9

questions.question: The word science is derived from _______word scientia.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (B): Latin. The word “science” comes from the Latin word scientia. It means knowledge or understanding.

questions.question: _________ is the study of matter, energy and their interaction.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (D): physics. Physics studies matter, energy and how they interact.It explains natural physical phenomenon.

questions.question: Least count of vernier caliper is _________.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): 0.01 cm. Least count is the smallest value a vernier caliper can measure. For a standard vernier caliper, it is 0.01 cm.

questions.question: One tera is equal to ______.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 10-12. The prefix “tera” represents 10 to the power of 12.It means one trillion.

questions.question: ________telescope orbits around the earth and provide information about stars.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): Hubble Space. The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth. It provides detailed Information about stars and galaxies.

questions.question: If zero line of Vernier scale is on the left side of the zero of the main scale then zero error is __________.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): positive. Left shift causes positive zero error.

questions.question: If zero of circular scale has crossed the index line, then zero error will be ___.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (C): zero. Crossed index means positive zero error. 36.Least count of digital balance is ____. (a) 0.01 mg (b) 0.001 mg (c) 1 mg ✓ (d) 0.1 mg EXPLANATION:Digital balance usually reads 1 mg. 37.If zero of circular scale is above the index line, then the zero error is to be ___. (a) added ✓ (b) subtracted (c) divided (d) multiplied EXPLANATION:: Above line, add error to reading.

questions.question: 0.00078 has ____significant figures.
questions.explanation: Correct Option (A): 4. Leading zeros are not significant; 7 and 8 count. 52.The diameter of thin wire can be measured by ____. (a) Vernier callipers (b) screw gauge ✓ (c) meter rule (d) measuring tape EXPLANATION: Screw gauge measures very small diameters accurately. 53.___ is the largest quantity from the following. (a) 0.01 g (b) 2 cm ✓ (c) 200 µg (d) 500 ng EXPLANATION: 2 cm is larger than the other small units. 54.A screw gauge has 80 divisions on its circular scale. The pitch of screw gauge is 0.5 mm. ___is the least count of screw gauge. (a) 0.001 mm (b) 0.06 mm (c) 0.01 mm ✓ (d) 0.006 mm EXPLANATION: Least count = Pitch / divisions = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm. 55.Least count of vernier caliper is also known as (a) Proportionality constant (b) vernier constant ✓ (c) pitch (d) vernier value (e) all of them EXPLANATION: Vernier constant is the same as least count. ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS CHAPTER: 01 MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS Q1. Which of the following sets include only base quantities? (a) Speed, force, energy (b) Time, mass, temperature ✓ (c)Velocity, acceleration, power (d)Work, momentum, torque Explanation: Time, mass, and temperature are base quantities. Q2. If density is a derived quantity, what could be the base quantities used to express it? (a)Mass and length ✓ (b)Time and length (c)Force and speed (d)Energy and work Explanation: Density depends on mass and volume. Q3. Which of the following is a base quantity? (a)Area (b)Power ( c)Length ✓ (d)Volume Explanation: Length is a fundamental base quantity. Q4. If you’re measuring the force exerted by a moving car, which base quantity are you considering? (a)Time (b)Mass ✓ ( c)Acceleration (d)Velocity Explanation: Force depends on mass and acceleration. Q5. Which of the following is a derived quantity? Time (a) Density ✓ (b) Temperature ( c) Length Explanation: Density is calculated from mass and volume. Q6. When measuring the work done by lifting a box, which base quantity are you assessing? (a) Force ✓ (b) Energy ( c) Power (d)Speed Explanation: Work depends on force and distance. Q7. If you’re calculating the speed of a runner, which base quantity are you utilizing? (a) Force (b) Mass ( c)Distance ✓ (d)Time ✓ Explanation: Speed uses distance and time. Q8. Which of the following is a derived quantity related to motion? (a) Mass (b) Velocity ✓ ( c)Temperature (d) Pressure Explanation: Velocity depends on distance and time. Q9. If you’re measuring the temperature of a substance, which base quantity are you evaluating? (a) Length (b)Time ( c)Mass (d)Temperature ✓ Explanation: Temperature is a base quantity. Q10. When determining the pressure inside a balloon, which base quantity are you considering? (a)Force ✓ (b)Length ( c)Temperature (d)Time Explanation: Pressure depends on force and area. Q11. Which of the following is a derived quantity associated with electricity? (a)Voltage ✓ (b)Mass ( c) Length (d)Temperature Explanation: Voltage is a derived electrical quantity. Q12. If you’re calculating the momentum of an object, which base quantity are you using? (a)Mass ✓ (b)Time ( c)Force (d)Length Explanation: Momentum depends on mass and velocity. Q13. Which of the following is a derived quantity in mechanics? (a)Energy ✓ (b)Length ( c)Time (d)Speed Explanation: Energy is calculated using force and distance. Q14. When measuring the energy consumption of a device, which base quantity are you examining? (a)Time ✓ (b)Mass ( c)Energy (d)Length Explanation: Energy consumption depends on time. Q15. If you’re determining the acceleration of a car, which base quantity are you finding? (a)Velocity (b)Time ✓ ( c)Force (d)Mass Explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time. Q16. Which of the following is NOT a derived unit in the SI system? (a)Newton (b)Pascal ( c)Ampere ✓ (d)Joule Explanation: Ampere is a base SI unit. Q17. A scientist is measuring the amount of substance in a chemical reaction. Which SI base unit will be appropriate? (a)Kelvin (b)Mole ✓ ( c)Candela (d)Ampere Explanation: Mole is the SI unit for amount of substance. Q18. Which of the following is a base unit for measuring time? (a)Meter (b)Second ✓ ( c)Kelvin (d)Ampere Explanation: Second is the SI base unit of time. Q19. What is the SI unit for measuring temperature? (a)Kelvin ✓ (b)Newton ( c)Pascal (d)Joule Explanation: Kelvin is the SI unit of temperature. Q20. Which SI unit is used to measure electric current? (a)Kelvin (b)Ampere ✓ ( c)Meter (d)Mole Explanation: Ampere is the SI unit of electric current. Q21. What is the SI unit for measuring luminous intensity? (a)Candela ✓ (b)Ampere ( c)Kilogram (d)Meter Explanation: Candela measures light intensity. Q22. Which SI unit measures the amount of substance? (a)Kelvin (b)Candela ( c)Mole ✓ (d)Newton Explanation: Mole measures the amount of substance. Q23. What is the SI unit for measuring mass? (a)Kilogram ✓ (b)Newton ( c)Meter (d)Ampere Explanation: Kilogram is the SI unit of mass. Q24. Which SI unit is used to measure distance? (a)Second (b)Meter ✓ ( c)Kilogram (d)Candela Explanation: Meter is the SI unit of length. Q25. What is the SI unit for measuring force? (a)Newton ✓ (b)Meter ( c)Ampere (d)Pascal Explanation: Newton is the SI unit of force. Q26. Which SI unit measures the brightness of light? ( a)Kelvin (b)Mole ( c)Candela ✓ (d)Ampere Explanation: Candela measures brightness of light. Q27. What is the SI unit for measuring energy? (a)Joule ✓ (b)Pascal ( c)Newton (d)Second Explanation: Joule is the SI unit of energy. Q28. Which SI unit is used to measure pressure? (a)Pascal ✓ (b)Kelvin ( c)Ampere (d)Candela Explanation: Pascal is the SI unit of pressure. Q29. What is the SI unit for measuring power? (a)Watt ✓ (b)Joule ( c)Newton (d)Meter Explanation: Watt is the SI unit of power. Q30. Which physical quantity has both magnitude and direction? (a)Mass (b)Time ( c)Force ✓ (d)Energy Explanation: Force is a vector quantity. Q31. If you push a box with a force of 10 N to the left, which represents the vector quantity? 10 N (a)Left (b)10 ( c)10 N towards the left ✓ Explanation: A vector includes both magnitude and direction. Q32. A vector of 7 units upward and another of 24 units to the right will have a resultant of: (a)17 units (b)25 units ✓ (c )31 units (d)20 units Explanation: Resultant = √(7² + 24²) = 25 units. Q33. When two vectors at right angles have the same magnitude, the resultant: (a)Equals one vector (b)Is twice one vector ( c)Is half one vector (d)Is √2 times one vector ✓ Explanation: Resultant of equal perpendicular vectors is √2 times one vector. Q34. Which tool is most suitable for measuring the length of a football field? (a)Micrometer (b)Vernier caliper ( c)Ruler (d)Measuring tape ✓ Explanation: Measuring tape is best for long distances. Q35. The main advantage of using a vernier caliper is: (a)Measures very large objects (b)Measures internal and external dimensions ✓ ( c)Always digital (d)Most basic tool Explanation: Vernier calipers measure both internal and external sizes. Q36. A micrometer is best used to measure: (a)Thickness of a book (b)Diameter of a hair ✓ ( c)Width of a table (d)Length of a rope Explanation: A micrometer measures very small thicknesses accurately. Q37. Which instrument provides the most precision for short time intervals? (a)Wall clock (b)Sundial ( c)Hourglass (d)Digital timer ✓ Explanation: Digital timers give very precise time readings. (Q38. To measure the time of 10 oscillations of a pendulum, the best tool is: (a)Grandfather clock (b)Digital stopwatch ✓ ( c)Hourglass ( d)Calendar Explanation: A digital stopwatch measures short time intervals accurately. Q39. A timer displaying 12.34 s shows precision up to: (a)1 s (b)1/10 s ( c)1/100 s ✓ (d)1/1000 s Explanation: Two decimal places mean precision of 1/100 s. Q40. What causes random error? (a)Bent ruler (b)Estimation ✓ ( c)Zero error (d)Slow stopwatch Explanation: Random error comes from estimation and unpredictable variation. Q41. Least count of an instrument means: (a)Maximum value (b)Average value ( c)Smallest measurable value ✓ (d)Estimated value Explanation: Least count is the smallest value an instrument can measure. Q42. Why are readings taken multiple times? (a)To complicate experiment (b)To get accurate average ✓ ( c)To waste time (d)To introduce error Explanation: Repeating readings reduces random error. Q43. Which indicates higher precision? (a)Large random error (b)Large systematic error ( c)Small random error ✓ (d)Zero error Explanation: Smaller random error means higher precision. Q44. Which statement is FALSE? (a)Precision means consistency (b)Accuracy means closeness to true value ( c)Precision always guarantees accuracy ✓ (d)Precise but inaccurate is possible Explanation: Precision does not always guarantee accuracy. Q45. A value that deviates greatly from others is called: (a)Consistent value (b)Systematic error ( c)Random error (d)Anomaly ✓ Explanation: A very different reading is called an anomaly. Q46. How many decimal places should 45.678 − 12.34 be rounded to? (a)1 (b)2 ( c)3 (d)4 ✓ Explanation: Result is rounded to the least decimal places used. Q47. Which is NOT a rule of significant figures? (a)Non-zero digits are significant (b)Zeros between digits are significant ( c)Leading zeros are significant ✓ (d)Trailing zeros in decimals are significant Explanation: Leading zeros are not significant. Q48. Which number has three significant figures? (a)1000 (b)0.00105 ✓ ( c)100.5 (d)1050 Explanation: 0.00105 has three significant figures. ADDITIONAL SHORT QUESTIONS
